samples.content: Title: "Cloudflare Workers AI llama-3.1-8b structured output". Topic: Cloudflare AI / LLM JSON mode. Found at https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/features/json-mode/. Summary: Workers AI now supports response_format with type 'json_schema'; pass the schema in the request payload and the model conforms to it. Saves a parsing layer. samples.summary: Cloudflare Workers AI now supports JSON mode, allowing users to pass a schema in the request payload and conform the model's output to it, eliminating the need for a parsing layer. This feature is available with the 'json_schema' response_format type.

samples.content: Research on mem0 conflict resolution: their LLM-resolver maps to four ops — ADD / UPDATE / DELETE / NOOP. Source: https://docs.mem0.ai/conflict-resolution. Key takeaway: keeping conflict resolution in the LLM (not pre-computed rules) trades determinism for adaptability. Engram should consider this for v0.2 conflict detection. Tags: mem0, conflict-resolution, llm, memory.
samples.summary: Mem0's LLM-resolver maps conflict resolution to four operations: ADD, UPDATE, DELETE, and NOOP, offering adaptability but trading determinism for a dynamic approach. This design consideration may influence Engram's v0.2 conflict detection implementation.

samples.content: Letta (formerly MemGPT) — self-edit memory mode. Title: Letta self-edit. URL: https://letta.com/blog/self-editing-memory. Summary: agents can call tools that rewrite their own memory blocks via patch operations. Risk: ungated self-edit becomes hallucination amplifier; Letta gates with a separate 'archival memory' tier. Engram should NOT adopt before v0.3 reflect ships. Tags: letta, memgpt, self-edit, agent-memory.
samples.summary: Letta's self-edit memory mode allows agents to rewrite their own memory blocks via patch operations, but is gated to prevent hallucination amplification through a separate 'archival memory' tier. This feature is currently not available in versions prior to v0.3 reflect ships.

samples.content: Notes on the MCP Resource Server pattern (2025-03-26 spec revision). The pattern uses /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource to advertise the Authorization Server's location. Bridge tools like mcp-remote expect this exact shape. Read at https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-03-26/oauth. Tags: mcp, oauth, resource-server, mcp-remote.
samples.summary: The MCP Resource Server pattern uses the /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource path to advertise the Authorization Server's location, as specified in the 2025-03-26 revision of the Model Context Protocol specification. This exact shape is expected by bridge tools like mcp-remote.

samples.content: Quick read on Vectorize namespaces (Cloudflare). Title: Vectorize namespaces tenant isolation. From https://developers.cloudflare.com/vectorize/best-practices/namespaces/. Key fact — one global index with namespace per workspace beats one-index-per-workspace because of the 100-index-per-account cap. Engram v0.1 must follow this. Tags: cloudflare, vectorize, namespaces, multi-tenant.
samples.summary: Cloudflare Vectorize recommends using one global index with a namespace per workspace for tenant isolation, as it avoids the 100-index-per-account cap, and this approach must be followed by Engram v0.1.

samples.content: Read this on the train — Anthropic's prompt-cache 5-minute TTL. Title: Claude API prompt cache TTL. Source: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#cache-lifetime. Summary: cache TTL is 5 minutes from last read; reads refresh it; expired blocks recompute on next request. Implication for Claude Code: keep wakeup intervals under 270s to stay in cache. Tags: anthropic, claude, prompt-cache, ttl, claude-code.
samples.summary: Anthropic's Claude API prompt-cache has a 5-minute TTL from last read, which is refreshed with each read and expired blocks are recomputed on the next request. To stay in the cache, Claude Code should keep wakeup intervals under 270 seconds.

samples.content: Title: Durable Objects SQLite migration footgun. Topic: Cloudflare DO storage. Source: https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/best-practices/migrations/. Summary: Once a DO class lands under new_sqlite_classes it CANNOT be moved back to new_classes — declaration is irreversible. Confirms Engram FND-08 CI lint rule. Tags: cloudflare, durable-objects, sqlite, migrations, irreversible.
samples.summary: When migrating a Durable Objects class to SQLite storage under new_sqlite_classes, the declaration is irreversible and the class cannot be moved back to new_classes. This confirms the Engram FND-08 CI lint rule.

samples.content: Notes from the agents SDK source dive: getAgentByName(namespace, name) returns a Promise<DurableObjectStub<T>> that MUST be awaited. Missing the await yields a Promise where the user expected a stub — subtle bug. Title: agents SDK getAgentByName pitfall. Topic: agents SDK + Durable Object stubs. No public URL — pulled from node_modules/agents/dist. Tags: agents-sdk, durable-objects, async, pitfall.
samples.summary: The `getAgentByName` function in the agents SDK returns a Promise that MUST be awaited, as missing the await can result in a Promise being returned instead of the expected stub, leading to a subtle bug.
